rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate all six compounds and identify critical pairs while limiting late-elution risk. The retention window will guide subsequent slope and temperature experiments.
Injection 1 already attained the maximum CRF of 1.000. Shorten the gradient by one grid step to seek a faster fully resolved method, retaining injection 1 as the optimal-score fallback.

The shorter gradient retains maximum CRF, but the critical pair is close to the resolution threshold. Raise temperature at fixed gradient to test whether selectivity improves while shortening retention.
At 50 C all pairs have resolution above 2, providing room to shorten the gradient. Test 6 minutes to find whether the faster method can retain the maximum CRF.

Reduce gradient steepness by lowering phi1 to restore the critical pair’s resolution while retaining a 6-minute gradient. The last peak previously eluted near phi 0.53, so phi1 0.80 leaves ample elution margin.

Shift the gradient window upward while preserving its slope to reduce retention without further gradient compression. This tests whether a higher starting organic fraction preserves the critical pair’s resolution and improves on injection 5’s time.

Raise the starting organic fraction another step to shorten retention, while slightly reducing the gradient slope to protect the critical pair. The earliest peaks remain sufficiently retained to justify testing this higher starting fraction.

Trim the gradient window and raise phi0 to shorten the run, using a slightly shallower slope to protect the critical pair. The previous last peak eluted near phi 0.51, so phi1 0.60 should provide sufficient elution strength.

Increase gradient steepness by one phi1 step to shorten the last-peak time while keeping initial retention unchanged. Injection 8’s minimum resolution of 1.85 provides some margin for this compression.

Restore injection 8’s shallower slope while shifting its window upward to shorten retention. This tests whether the higher starting fraction preserves both the early-pair separation and the critical middle pair.

Lower phi1 one step to spread the critical middle pair while preserving injection 10’s acceptable early-pair separation. This may recover full resolution with a last-peak time shorter than injection 8.

With maximum CRF already secured, test a much steeper gradient for a faster separation beyond a possible middle-pair elution-order reversal. Lower temperature and phi0 should help preserve early-pair retention and resolution.

Return to the fastest fully resolved method and test a 5 C temperature increase for shorter retention and improved middle-pair selectivity. Monitor the early pair closely, since previous warming reduced its separation.

Test lower-temperature selectivity with a steep gradient to see whether the reordered middle pair can separate on a faster branch. Maximum CRF is already secured; this exploratory run targets a shorter fully resolved alternative.

Test a higher starting organic fraction at low temperature to alter middle-pair selectivity without the severe compression of the 2-minute gradient. Lower temperature should help retain the early compounds as the gradient window shifts upward.

Test a higher starting fraction with a shallower gradient to restore middle-pair resolution while shortening the retention window. Cooling slightly from 50 C should protect the early pair, which became limiting at 55 C.

Test whether a higher-organic window at low temperature separates the middle pair after an elution-order reversal, using a shallow slope to limit compression. This is exploratory; injection 11 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-CRF method.

Increase slope at fixed starting composition and temperature to test whether the reversed middle pair gains selectivity while the late peaks elute faster. Injection 17 leaves substantial resolution margin in every other pair.

The middle pair barely responded to slope, so shift the starting composition upward to test selectivity instead. This may improve its separation and shorten retention, although the early pair is likely to become limiting.

Return to phi0 0.40, where the early pair had resolution margin, and test temperature selectivity at fixed gradient. The aim is to lift the middle pair above 1.5 without losing the short retention time of injection 18.

Refine the successful 50 C region with a slope between injections 8 and 9, targeting full resolution near the shortest confirmed retention time. The lower starting fraction should preserve more early-pair resolution than injection 11.

Test a slightly shallower gradient around the fastest confirmed maximum-CRF method to increase its narrow middle-pair resolution margin. The endpoint remains above the estimated last-peak elution fraction, so the modest time increase should stay well below the scoring penalty threshold.

Lower temperature one step from injection 22 to improve early-pair separation while using its middle-pair resolution margin. This tests a potentially more robust maximum-CRF alternative, with retention still comfortably below 10 minutes.

Increase phi1 one step from injection 23 to shorten retention while using its middle-pair resolution margin. This also tests whether the fastest confirmed method remains fully resolved at a 5 C lower temperature.

Use a slope between injections 11 and 22 to target maximum CRF with more middle-pair resolution margin than the fastest confirmed method. This untested grid combination should retain all six compounds well within 10 minutes.
